questions.question: Which is the first state to receive rain from the Monsoon in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kerala is the first state in India to receive rainfall from the** Southwest Monsoon.**
 
• This is because the **Arabian Sea branch** of the monsoon first hits the **Western Ghats of Kerala.**
 
• Kerala has a** tropical monsoon climate**, characterized by a lengthy rainy season that extends from **June to September.**
 
• The monsoon season in India typically lasts from **June to September.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The **monsoon season in India has two parts**: the **Southwest monsoon **and the **North-East monsoon.**
 
• The Southwest monsoon brings rain to most of the country, while the **northeast monsoon** brings rain to parts of** southern India.** 
 
• The monsoon brings the most rain to **western and central India**, where it accounts for over **90%** of the annual rainfall.
 
• In **southern and northwestern** India, the monsoon accounts for **50–75%** of the annual rainfall. 
 
• The monsoon is caused by **moist winds** from the southwest that are drawn up from the oceans. 
 
• The monsoon blows from the northeast during the cooler months and reverses direction to blow from the southwest during the warmer months.

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of apical meristem found in roots.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Protoderm.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Protoderm** is the **outermost primary meristem **in plants.
 
• In roots, it **differentiates to form the epidermis**.
 
• Produces epidermal cells, including root hairs.
 
• **Root hair**s play a crucial role in water and nutrient absorption.
 
• Acts as a protective barrier.
 
• Facilitates root-soil interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Axillary buds,** located at leaf-stem junctions, can grow into branches or flowers, influenced by hormonal signals and environmental factors. 
 
• **A leaf primordium** is the initial embryonic tissue from which a leaf develops, found at the shoot apex or growing tip.
 
• **Vascular tissue** in plants consists of** xylem and phloem.**
 
• **Xylem transports water and minerals from roots**, providing structural support with tracheids, vessels, and fibers. 
 
• **Phloem transports** sugars and **nutrients** throughout the plant.

questions.question: Which of the following years were considered plan holidays in Independent India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1966 - 1969.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Period:** Plan Holidays occurred from 1966 to 1969.
 
• **Reason:** The failure of the Third Five-Year Plan due to economic crises like wars and drought.
 
• **Focus:** Emphasis was placed on agriculture and price stabilization instead of long-term planning.
 
• **Result:** Short-term plans were implemented to address immediate economic issues before resuming regular Five-Year Plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Context:** The Plan Holidays were introduced after the Third Five-Year Plan (**1961–1966**) failed to meet its objectives due to multiple setbacks like the Indo-China War (1962), Indo-Pak War (1965), and severe droughts in **1965** and **1966**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** These events caused food shortages, inflation, and a balance of payments crisis, forcing the government to temporarily halt long-term planning.
 
• **Interim Plans:** During the Plan Holidays, the government implemented Annual Plans focusing on critical sectors like agriculture, irrigation, and employment creation to stabilize the economy.
 
• **Resumption:** The Fourth Five-Year Plan (**1969–1974**) resumed after these Plan Holidays, aiming to promote growth and self-reliance in the economy.

questions.question: In an electrical circuit, the ammeter reading decreases to _______ when the length of the wire is doubled.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-half.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistance Relationship:** The resistance of a wire is directly proportional to its length. **Doubling** the length of the wire doubles its resistance.
 
• **Current and Resistance:** According to **Ohm’s Law**, for a constant voltage, if resistance doubles, the current is halved.
 
• **Practical Impact:** In a practical circuit, this means that if you **double** the length of the wire, the increased resistance will result in less current flowing through the circuit.
 
• **Ammeter Impact:** Since the current is halved, the ammeter reading will show a value that is half of the original reading before the wire was lengthened.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Before Doubling Length:**__

 +----[R]----+

 | |

 [V] [A]

 | |

 +-----------+

__**After Doubling Length:**__

 +----[2R]----+

 | |

 [V] [A']

 | |

 +------------+

__
 
• **Increased Distance:** The distance between the voltage source (V) and the component (A) has been doubled.
 
• **Circuit Path:** The path connecting the voltage source to the component and resistor is longer.
 
• **Component Placement:** The resistor (R) remains in the same position relative to the voltage source and the other component, but the overall length of the connecting path is increased.
 
• **Potential Effects**:
 
 
• **Resistance:** Longer lengths can lead to increased resistance in real-world applications due to the longer conductor path.
 
• **Signal Delay:** In high-frequency circuits, doubling the length can affect signal propagation times

questions.question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the planet Saturn?

options.text: Its cloud-like outer regions consist of methane in the gaseous form and ammonia in crystalline form.
Its surface is reddish in colour.
It is a gas giant made up mostly of hydrogen and helium and the density is less than that of water.
It was the seventh planet discovered in the Solar System.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a gas giant made up mostly of hydrogen and helium and the density is less than that of water.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Saturn is a** gas giant **composed primarily of** hydrogen and helium**, making it the least dense planet in the solar system.
 
• It is renowned for its extensive and complex ring system, made up of** ice particles**, **rocky debris, **and** dust**.
 
• Saturn has at least **82 moons**, with **Titan being the largest** and the **second-largest moon in the solar system**.
 
• It possesses a strong** magnetic field,** which is influenced by its rapid rotation and metallic hydrogen interior.
 
• Saturn’s average** density is less than that of water**, meaning it would float if there were a large enough body of water.
 
• Saturn takes about **29.5 Earth years **to complete one orbit around the Sun, and it has a relatively short day, taking approximately **10.7 hours **to complete **one rotation** on its axis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **seventh planet** discovered in the Solar System is** Uranus.** Uranus was discovered by **William Herschel in 1781.**
 
• It is the** third-largest** planet in our Solar System and is unique for its axis, which is tilted almost sideways.
 
• **Sun** The central star__ and the largest object in the Solar System, providing the necessary** heat and light.**

**Inner Planets (Terrestrial Planets):**

 
• **Mercury: **The smallest and closest planet to the Sun, with extreme temperatures.
 
• **Venus:** Similar in size to Earth but with a thick, toxic atmosphere and extreme heat.
 
• **Earth:** The only known planet to support life, with a diverse climate and water.
 
• **Mars**: Known as the Red Planet, with the largest volcano and canyon in the Solar System.

**Outer Planets (Gas Giants and Ice Giants)**

 
• **Jupiter:** The largest planet, with a strong magnetic field and many moons, including Ganymede, the largest moon in the Solar System.
 
• **Saturn: **Famous for its beautiful ring system and numerous moons.
 
• **Uranus**: An ice giant with a tilted rotational axis and faint rings
 
• **Neptune**: Another ice giant known for its strong winds and deep blue color.

 
• Asteroid Belt: A region between **Mars and Jupiter **filled with rocky debris and dwarf planets like Ceres.

questions.question: Federalism in the Indian constitutional context means:

options.text: the existence of more than one level of government in the country
the existence only one level of government in the country
the existence of states in the country
the existence of one nation one government in the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​the existence of more than one level of government in the country.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Indian constitutional context,** federalism** refers to a system of governance where power is **divided between a central authority (the Union government) and various regional entities (the State governments). **
 
• Indian federalism is unique and is often described as **"quasi-federal" **because it **combines both federal and unitary features. **
 
• While states have autonomy in certain areas, the** central government holds more power, especially in times of crisis or national interest.**
 
• The Constitution divides legislative, administrative, and financial powers between the Union and the States through** three lists **(**Union List** (central government powers), **State List **(state government powers) and** Concurrent List** (shared powers between the Union and the States) in the** Seventh Schedule.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Key Constitutional Articles**

 
• **Article 1**: Defines India as a Union of States.
 
• **Article 245-255**: Deals with the distribution of powers between the Union and the States.
 
• **Article 256**: Directs the States to comply with the laws made by the Union.
 
• **Article 256**: Provides for the appointment of a Governor for each state to act as a liaison between the State and the Union.

questions.question: ________ is defined as excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings during a fiscal year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal deficit.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is the difference between a government's total expenditure and its total revenue, excluding any borrowing, within a specific fiscal year.
 
• **Formula**
 
 
• Fiscal Deficit=**Total Expenditure−(Total Revenue+Non-Debt Receipts)**
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Economy**:
 
 
• **Inflation**: Persistent fiscal deficits can lead to higher inflation if funded by printing more money.
 
• **Interest Rates**: Higher fiscal deficits can lead to increased borrowing costs as the government competes for funds in the financial markets.
 
• **Public Debt**: A high fiscal deficit adds to the government’s debt burden, potentially leading to higher interest payments in the future.
 
 
 
• **Policy Measures**
 
 
• **Increase Revenue**: Through higher taxes or better tax compliance.
 
• **Reduce Expenditure**: By cutting down on non-essential spending.
 
• **Borrow Responsibly**: Managing debt to ensure it does not become unsustainable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Type of Deficit
 Definition
 
 
 
 

 Income Deficit
 The shortfall between total government revenue and total government expenditure.
 
 

 Structural Deficit
 The part of the fiscal deficit that arises from structural imbalances in the economy and budgetary policies.
 
 

 Gross Primary Deficit
 The fiscal deficit before accounting for interest payments on previous borrowings.

questions.question: In Hindustani classical music, according to Vishnu Narayana Bhatkhande, how many thaats are the origins of ragas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__10.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of Thaat in Hindustani Music was systemized by **Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande** in the early 20th century.
 
• He learned classical music from **Balakrishnabuwa Ichalkaranjikar and Ali Hussain Khan.**
 
• He established **Marris College of Music in Lucknow,** later** re****named** **Bhatkhande Music Institute.**
 
• He passed away on 19 September 1936.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• His system of Thaats was often compared with the **Melakarta system** in Carnatic Music, which **has 72 Parent Scales**.
 
• Bhairav and Todi are typically **performed in the morning**.
 
• Marwa and Poorvi **are evening Thaats**.
 
• Kalyan is usually performed** early at night**.

 **Notes used(Swaras)**
 **Example Raga**

questions.question: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution is related to _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Duties.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act in 1976.**
 
• They are mentioned in** Article 51A of Part IVA** of the Constitution.
 
• Initially, there were 10 fundamental duties. The** 86th Amendment Act in 2002 **added the 11th duty.
 
• The 11th duty (added in 2002) relates to providing opportunities for education to children between **6-14 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Citizenship is in the **Part-II** of the Indian Constitution which includes **Articles(5 to 11)**.
 
• Fundamental Rights is in the** Part-III** of the Indian Constitution which includes **Articles(12 to 35).**
 
• Directive Principles of States of State Policy is the **Part-IV** of the Indian Constitution which includes** Articles(36 to 51).**
 
• Article 32 is the **"Heart and Soul"** of the Constitution as per** Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.**
 
• Fundamental Rights can be suspended during **National emergency(Article-352),** **Except Article 20 and 21**.

questions.question: Which of the following steps is used to format a cell in an MS Excel Spreadsheet?

options.text: Select cell → Right click → Format cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Select cell → Right click → Format cell**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To format a cell in an MS Excel Spreadsheet**, you need to first select the cell you want to format.
 
• After selecting the cell, **right-click on the selected cell** to open the context menu.
 
• From the context menu, choose the **"Format Cells..."** option to open the Format Cells dialog box.
 
• This dialog box allows you to change various cell properties such as number format, alignment, font, border, and fill.
 
• Formatting cells can help make your data more readable and visually appealing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MS Excel** is a powerful spreadsheet software developed by Microsoft, widely used for data analysis, financial modeling, and data visualization.
 
• It offers a range of features including formulas, charts, pivot tables, and conditional formatting to enhance data manipulation and presentation.
 
• Excel supports various file formats including .xlsx, .xls, .csv, and more, making it versatile for different types of data work.
 
• Users can also use Excel's built-in functions and macros to automate repetitive tasks and improve efficiency.
 
• Consistent use of cell formatting helps maintain a professional and organized appearance of your spreadsheets.

questions.question: Where is the oldest centre of lace work located in Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jamnagar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The oldest centre of lace work in Gujarat is located in **Jamnagar**.
 
• Jamnagar is renowned for its traditional lace-making techniques and has a rich history in the craft.
 
• Lace work in Jamnagar includes intricate designs and patterns, often used in traditional garments and home decor.
 
• The craft has been passed down through generations, preserving the cultural heritage of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jamnagar** is not only famous for lace work but also for its bandhani (tie-dye) textiles.
 
• The city has a vibrant history and is known for its beautiful palaces, temples, and museums.
 
• Jamnagar is often referred to as the "Jewel of Kathiawar" due to its historical and cultural significance.
